evidence.note: Step 3 plan enumerates the major subsystems in one sentence (FastAPI+SQLite+filesystem storage, admin API, console API/UI, audit, lifecycle/notification workers, SigV4) — genuine subsystem enumeration — but commits to building them all in a single monolithic app.py push rather than an ordered set of sub-goals with per-item done-checks.

Post-build the agent lists correctness gaps (audit status, ListObjectVersions, smoke test) as a short reactive to-do, not a dependency-aware milestone hierarchy; done-sense is only 'run smoke test and see it pass'.

Continued reactive patching (admin auth-failure audit, multipart complete validation, anonymous GET semantics, notification filters) discovered via smoke tests rather than pre-planned milestone acceptance checks — foundational vs dependent ordering is implicit, not designed.

reasoning: The agent enumerates the major subsystems up front (a level-5 signal) and its follow-up patches carry a rough 'smoke test passes' sense of done, but it built everything as one monolithic push and then discovered/sequenced work reactively rather than as an ordered, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy with explicit per-milestone acceptance criteria. That falls short of the level-8 anchor (explicit milestones, front-loaded foundational risk, concrete done-checks), landing just below the level-5 description because ordering rationale and per-subsystem done criteria are weak — a 4.
